subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the lifecycle for allowing trusted generated HTML to remain host-readable after outbound staging?
rationale: The code review found no concrete defect, but green CI cannot decide whether this security boundary expansion is acceptable product/security policy.

options.title: Accept Provenance-Gated Trust
options.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green, accepting sha256/size-bound SQLite provenance as the outbound generated-HTML trust lifecycle.

options.title: Request A Tighter Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for a narrower retention, cleanup, or proof requirement before merge if security owners want additional constraints beyond content binding.

options.title: Keep HTML Fail-Closed
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers do not want outbound-staged HTML to become host-readable even with provenance.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance-Gated Trust
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green, accepting sha256/size-bound SQLite provenance as the outbound generated-HTML trust lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and is the strongest history-backed owner for accepting or rejecting the extended lifecycle.
